condition_other: obesity (leptin-receptor knockout db/db mice; high-fat diet)
readout_other: food intake; body weight; serum glucose and lipids (ELISA); c-Fos immunofluorescence in ARC with POMC/NPY colocalisation; whole-cell current-clamp of POMC and NPY neurons in slices
direction_notes: ARC stimulation at PRF 500 Hz, DC 50% increased c-Fos and POMC neuron firing and reduced food intake and body weight gain; the 1.5 kHz, 10% set and V1 stimulation did not change food intake.
safety_notes: Authors state no negative effects were observed in mice and that UDBS did not cause motor or mental disorders (Fig. S5).

timing.protocol_description: Two parameter sets in the acute experiment: PRF 500 Hz, DC 50%, TBD 1 ms; and PRF 1.5 kHz, DC 10%, TBD 0.067 ms; sonication duration 1 s, inter-stimulus interval 2 s (5 s in the HFD and transgenic experiments, PRF 500 Hz set only). Acute sessions 15 min; subacute 1 h/day for 2 days; db/db mice 15 min/day for 10 days then 33 days of 15 min/day; HFD mice 15 min every 2 days, 14 times.
V1 control: TBD 1 ms and PRF 500 Hz (the 50% duty cycle set), 15 min, same sonication duration, interval and pressure as the acute ARC experiment; only this set was tested at V1.

source_quotes.n_subjects: Mice received ultrasound stimulation in ARC (n = 8) or V1 (n = 7) for 15 min, followed by measurement of food intake every 30 min for 2 h.

flags.reason: 586 kPa is called 'acoustic pressure'; a hydrophone measured inside the skull and the paper reports 54% skull attenuation at 3.8 MHz, but does not say whether 586 kPa is free-field or in the brain.
Group sizes differ per experiment (acute ARC 8, V1 7, subacute 8, db/db 13 per group, HFD 9) and animal reuse is unclear; only the acute groups are listed.
The paper states TBD 1 ms and PRF 500 Hz for V1; the 50% duty cycle is taken from the acute parameter set that applied to V1.
Burst rule: TBD 1 ms with PRF 500 Hz and DC 50% is consistent (1 ms x 500 Hz = 50%); TBD is the pulse.
Sham: ultrasound output abolished (inactive transducer); V1 stimulation acts as an active control site.
